## Shared teaching example

The workshop uses `HealthWellbeing` from
[section 4.2.4, Correlations](https://doing-meta.guide/pooling-es#correlations),
of *Doing Meta-Analysis with R: A Hands-On Guide* by Harrer, Cuijpers, Furukawa,
and Ebert (2021). The dataset contains 29 study-level summaries, with the fields
`author`, `cor`, `n`, `population`, and `country`.

Follow this dataset from source attribution and environment preparation through
metadata, storage, analysis, reporting, and archiving. The
[workshop teaching plan](workshop_plan.qmd) gives the full learning objectives
and delivery guidance. This page is an unpublished planning document.

## Structure within a practical page

Use learning objectives, a short explanation of why the step matters, a worked
example, one participant action, an expected-result checkpoint, key takeaways,
and further reading. Opening, archiving, and closing pages can use a short
demonstration or discussion instead of a full practical exercise.

Use prepared inputs and fallback outputs to keep activities within their time
allocation. Complete installations, downloads, and image builds before the
session. Keep the closing discussion even if optional demonstrations are skipped.

## Supplied examples for the optional closing page

Retain the supplied snippets as the basis for page 09, with the
preparation in this order:

1. Load the verified `HealthWellbeing` snapshot, either from the raw file used
   throughout the workshop or from `dmetar` when that package is available.
2. Define `original` with a factor `population`, `z = atanh(cor)`, and
   `log_n = log(n)`. Both optional examples depend on this object.
3. Use `synthpop::syn()` with CART and seed 123; convert synthetic `z` and
   `log_n` back with `tanh()` and rounded `exp()`; generate synthetic study
   labels; inspect distributions with `compare()`. Label all generated records
   as synthetic, including their generated sample sizes.
4. Fit the illustrative regressions `z ~ population` and
   `z ~ population + log_n`. Store them using `vetiver_model()` and
   `vetiver_pin_write()` on a versioned local `pins` board named `model_store`,
   with the model name `health_wellbeing`.
5. Inspect `pin_versions()` and demonstrate `vetiver_pin_read()`. The supplied
   read retrieves the latest version; reproducible follow-up should record and
   retrieve a specified version and link it to the training data and environment.

These unweighted regressions illustrate model storage and alternative
specifications; they are not the correlation meta-analysis taught in the core
pipeline. The synthesis example is not a differential privacy guarantee, and a
distribution comparison does not establish one. Both examples share the final
five-minute slot with discussion; fuller execution belongs in follow-up material.

## Development and validation status

Only pages 00–03 are being added in the current authoring task. The remaining
pages and their dependencies need implementation and validation. The current
lockfile records renv 1.0.7 under R 4.4.1; do not infer that the packages named
in the plan have already been installed or locked.

Codex assisted with this page plan and the initial chapters. Agent checks do
not constitute human review; human review is pending.
